subject_line: Wall mice and hermit thrushes in The Complete Stories
email_body:
Dear Noah,

I've been reading about The Complete Stories, your Copper Canyon follow-up to The Destroyer in the Glass, and was struck by how "Wall Mice," "Trash Day" and "Hermit Thrush" sit beside a title poem that seems to promise a whole fiction.

I'd like to ask how the broken forms in this book came about, and whether working through grief in those shapes felt different from writing your first collection.

The Author Ledger is an independent project featuring short Author Spotlights. The portrait is developed through a few written questions, which you can answer at your own pace, and the full text is shared with you for review before publication.

Would you be open to taking part? No pressure either way.

Best regards,
The Author Ledger

Dear Susan,

Landslide caught my attention for the way it stays in a Maine fishing community after the accident that leaves Jill's husband hospitalized across the border in Canada, and she is left at home with two teenage sons.

I'd love to ask how your years co-founding the Telling Room, working with young writers in Portland, shaped the voices of those boys on the page.

subject_line: Memoir, documentary and criticism in Lowest White Boy
email_body:
Dear Greg,

Lowest White Boy, your book in West Virginia University Press's In Place series, interests me because it is described as memoir, documentary and criticism at once, and you were the first creative writing professor at UVM to specialize in creative nonfiction.

I'd like to explore how you decide which of those three modes leads in a given chapter, and whether teaching nonfiction has changed how you mix them.
